title: Spotlight indexing
explanation: Builds the search index after files change. Normal for a few minutes after big copies or updates.

title: Window server
explanation: Draws every window on your screen and sends your clicks and keys to the right app. Busy with many windows or large displays.

title: Photos analysis
explanation: Scans your photo library in the background to find people, places and objects for search. Normal after you add many photos.

title: macOS core
explanation: The core of macOS. It also holds back the CPU on purpose to cool a hot Mac, so high use here is usually not a fault.

title: Time Machine backup
explanation: Makes Time Machine backups and keeps their history. Busy while a backup runs.

title: Spotlight file scanning
explanation: Reads new and changed files so Spotlight can search them. Many can run at once after updates or big copies.

title: Software updates
explanation: Runs macOS software updates. Busy for a while when an update downloads or installs.

title: iCloud sync
explanation: Syncs app data with iCloud. Busy when apps change a lot of data or after you sign in.

title: iCloud Drive
explanation: Keeps your iCloud Drive files in sync. Busy during big uploads or downloads.

title: Background transfers
explanation: Does downloads and uploads for apps while they are in the background. Busy when apps sync or fetch large files.

title: Tabs and sites
explanation: Draws the pages, tabs and windows of the app. Each open tab or site often runs in its own.

title: Graphics
explanation: Draws the app's graphics and video with the graphics chip. An app usually has one.

title: Extensions
explanation: Runs the app's extensions and plug-ins apart from the main app.

title: Helpers
explanation: Does background jobs for the app. Its memory and CPU count toward the app.

title: Google Chrome
explanation: Google's web browser. Tabs, extensions and graphics run as separate helper processes that count toward Chrome.

title: Safari
explanation: Apple's web browser. Web pages and tabs run as separate processes that count toward Safari.

title: Slack
explanation: Team chat app. It is built like a web browser, so it runs several helper processes and can use a lot of memory.

title: Xcode
explanation: Apple's app for building software. Builds, indexing and previews can use a lot of memory and CPU.

title: Claude
explanation: The Claude chat app. It is built like a web browser, so it runs several helper processes.

title: Finder
explanation: Shows your files and folders and draws the desktop. macOS restarts it at once if it quits.
